title: Set 317

sentences.ko: 엄청 좋은 스탠딩 책상을 하나 샀거든. 근데 진짜 맹세하는데 서서 쓴 건 한 일주일이 다야. 지금은 그냥 앉는 높이에 박혀 있고, 상자를 벌써 버려서 반품도 못 해.
sentences.text: I bought one of those really nice standing desks, and I swear I stood at it for like a week. Now it's just stuck at sitting height, and I can't even return it because I already threw out the box.

alts.text: Got one of those fancy standing desks, and I swear I stood at it maybe a week. Now it never goes up, and I can't even send it back 'cause I tossed the box.

I purchased one of those very nice standing desks, and I honestly stood at it for only about a week. It now stays at sitting height, and I am unable to return it because I have already discarded the box.

sentences.note: **I swear** 는 진짜야, 맹세해 라는 뜻으로 말에 힘을 줄 때 써요. **threw out** 은 버렸다는 말이고, 캐주얼에서는 **tossed** 를 써요.

sentences.ko: 우리 계속 도시를 떠날까 하는 얘기를 해. 거기 가면 마당 있는 집도 진짜 살 수 있거든. 근데 그러면 편도로 한 시간씩 출퇴근해야 하는데, 솔직히 마당이 그만한 가치가 있는지 모르겠어.
sentences.text: We keep talking about moving out of the city, because we could actually afford a place with a yard out there. But then I'd have an hour commute each way, and I honestly don't know if a yard is worth that.

alts.text: We keep saying we should leave the city, 'cause out there we could actually afford a place with a yard. But then I'd be commuting an hour each way, and I dunno if a yard's worth that.

We continue to discuss moving out of the city, because we could actually afford a home with a yard there. However, I would then have a one-hour commute in each direction, and I am genuinely unsure whether a yard is worth that.

sentences.note: **an hour commute each way** 는 편도로 한 시간 걸려 출퇴근한다는 말이에요. **worth that** 은 그만한 가치가 있다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 그 사람이 처음 만나면 좀 조용한데, 한 10분만 지나 봐, 알고 보면 진짜 웃겨. 그리고 선생님이라서 애들이랑 엄청 잘 지내. 너한테 그게 중요한 거 나도 알거든.
sentences.text: So he's kind of quiet when you first meet him, but give it like ten minutes and he's actually really funny. And he's a teacher, so he's great with kids, which I know is a big thing for you.

alts.text: He's kinda quiet at first, but give him like ten minutes and he's actually super funny. Plus he's a teacher, so he's great with kids, and I know that's a big deal for you.

He is somewhat quiet when you first meet him, but after about ten minutes you will find that he is actually very funny. He is also a teacher, so he is wonderful with children, which I understand is very important to you.

sentences.note: **give it like ten minutes** 는 한 10분만 기다려 봐 라는 뜻이에요. **a big thing for you** 는 너한테 중요한 일이라는 말이고, 캐주얼에서는 **a big deal** 이라고 해요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 오늘 밤에 애 재우는 데 한 시간 반 걸렸어. 잠들었나 싶어서 살금살금 나가려고 할 때마다 바닥이 삐걱거리고, 그럼 애가 다시 벌떡 일어나 앉는 거야.
sentences.text: It took me an hour and a half to get her down tonight. Every time I thought she was asleep, I'd try to sneak out, and then the floor would creak and she'd sit right back up again.

alts.text: Took me an hour and a half to get her to sleep tonight. Every time I thought she was out, I'd try to sneak off, and the floor would creak and boom, she's sitting up again.

It took me an hour and a half to get her to sleep this evening. Each time I believed she was asleep, I attempted to leave quietly, and then the floor would creak and she would sit up again immediately.

sentences.note: **get her down** 은 아이를 재운다는 말이에요. **sneak out** 은 몰래 빠져나가다, **creak** 는 바닥이나 문이 삐걱거리는 소리예요.

sentences.ko: 아, 나 드디어 차고 정리했어. 주말 내내 걸렸어. 하다가 중간에 할머니 옛날 편지가 든 상자를 찾았거든. 그래서 결국 마무리는 안 하고 바닥에 앉아서 그 편지들만 읽고 있었어.
sentences.text: Oh, I finally cleaned out the garage. It took me the whole weekend, because halfway through I found a box of my grandma's old letters, and I ended up sitting on the floor reading them instead of actually finishing.

alts.text: Oh, garage is finally clean! Took all weekend, 'cause halfway in I found a box of my grandma's old letters, and I just ended up sitting on the floor reading them instead of finishing.

I have finally cleaned out the garage. It took me the entire weekend, because partway through I discovered a box of my grandmother's old letters, and I ended up sitting on the floor reading them rather than finishing the task.

sentences.note: **cleaned out** 은 안에 있는 것을 꺼내 싹 정리한다는 뜻이에요. **ended up** 은 그럴 생각은 없었는데 결국 그렇게 됐다는 말이에요.

reviewed: 1번 casual 의 used it standing 은 어색해서 stood at it 으로 고치고, 영어 앞부분과 덜 겹치게 바꿈
1번 formal 의 I believe 는 I swear 의 강조를 추측으로 바꿔 뜻이 약해져서 honestly 로 고침
1번 한국어의 쓴 건 한 일주일쯤인 것 같아 는 영어에 없는 추측 말투라서 맹세하는 느낌으로 고침
2번 formal 의 one hour commute 를 one-hour commute 로 고침
2번 한국어가 마당 하나 때문에 그럴 가치 로 꼬여 있어서 자연스럽게 다듬음
3번 한국어의 중요한 거 알잖아 는 영어의 which I know (나도 알고 있다)와 뜻이 달라서 고침
4번 formal 의 put her to bed 는 눕히는 것이고 get her down 은 재우는 것이라 get her to sleep 으로 고침
